report.summary: Two findings: session tokens (a Restricted asset) are now persisted in a new external Redis store that the threat model does not represent, plus an unmodeled new third-party dependency github.com/redis/go-redis/v9.

findings.title: Restricted session tokens now stored in an unmodeled external Redis cache

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "session tokens" classification=Restricted — Bearer tokens proving a signed-in session

evidence.note: New Cache type stores session tokens in Redis so instances share log-ins — a data store not present in the model
redis.NewClient(&redis.Options{Addr: addr}) — no TLS and no password/ACL configured for the connection carrying Restricted tokens
Put writes key "session:"+token holding userID, i.e. the raw bearer token is the storage key (no hashing)

relevance.justification: The model's only Restricted information asset is now written to and read from a brand-new external store with no modeled trust boundary or protection.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the threat model "login service": this PR added internal/session/cache.go, which persists the Restricted "session tokens" information asset in an external Redis instance (redis.NewClient with only an Addr — no TLS, no auth) using the raw bearer token as the key ("session:"+token). Add a data_flow_diagram (or dfd block) with a data_store "session cache (Redis)" plus flows from the login service process to it carrying the "session tokens" asset across a trust zone boundary, and add a threat covering compromise or sniffing of the session cache (STRIDE Spoofing/Information disclosure) with controls describing the intended Redis TLS/AUTH configuration and whether tokens are stored hashed; mark those controls implemented = false until the code sets them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Redis session-cache data store, its flows for the "session tokens" asset, and a threat/controls for cache compromise in app.tm.hcl.

findings.title: New third-party dependency go-redis has no third_party_dependency assertion

model_excerpt.quote: third_party_dependency "identity provider" uptime_dependency=degraded — Hosted IdP handling SSO log-ins

evidence.note: go-redis imported to back session storage, making Redis availability required for session lookup

relevance.justification: The model lists only the IdP as a third-party dependency, yet session resolution now depends on a newly added Redis client library and server.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: this PR added github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 v9.7.0 (go.mod:6) and internal/session/cache.go, which resolves every session token through Redis. Add a third_party_dependency block "session cache (Redis)" with a description noting it stores bearer tokens and an appropriate uptime_dependency value (Get failures block session resolution, so "operational" is likely correct unless there is a fallback), so the model reflects the new external dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third_party_dependency "session cache (Redis)" block to app.tm.hcl with the appropriate uptime_dependency.
